ev.q: Rate ratios and 95% CIs were calculated to compare racial/ethnic groups in each 3-year interval.
To produce stable mortality estimates, diabetes death rates were analyzed in 3-year intervals.
During 2012–2014, black children and adolescents had the highest diabetes death rate (2.04 per 1 million population)
During 2000–2002, the diabetes death rate ratio for blacks compared with whites was 2.36
CDC analyzed data from the National Vital Statistics System for deaths among persons aged 1–19 years
From 2000–2002 to 2012–2014, the annual percentage change in diabetes death rate among all children and adolescents was -1.7%.

methods_quotes.q: Joinpoint regression was used based on 3-year intervals to analyze trends using Hudson’s algorithm, which includes time as a continuous variable
Joinpoint regression uses permutation tests to identify points where linear trends change significantly in direction or magnitude
The rate of change was tested for each trend to determine whether it was significantly different from zero
Rate ratios and 95% CIs were calculated to compare racial/ethnic groups in each 3-year interval.
